propositions: Core command handlers across ticket, store, read/write, config, import/export, maintenance, and gate families currently parse argv imperatively without centralized grammar definitions, creating duplication that migrating to shared argparse factories would eliminate.

Each migrated command must route its _dispatch_* handler through a per-family S2a parser factory wired onto its Route.parser_factory field, with per-family unknown-token semantics (skip vs reject-exit-2) preserved and global flags extracted only at the router level.

Parser factories must accept argv matrices covering missing/surplus arguments, space/equal options, --, and malformed input while producing byte-exact parity in acceptance/rejection, exit codes, diagnostics, and persisted effects versus pre-migration behavior.

Parser construction must not import domain executors or optional dependencies, and real production-path execution must resolve only the selected parser factory and handler, provable via construction-exclusion probes and dispatch-isolation assertions.

Each command family (parser module + single _registry.py wiring line + _dispatch_* switch) must form a self-contained, revertable unit with no cross-family coupling and must comply with module-size and complexity policy limits.
